_GeneralInformation.ShortName: California RC Bridges 2025 (Chen et al.) - Bridge Components, EDP-based
_GeneralInformation.Description: Seismic fragility models for the components of California reinforced concrete bridges, conditioned on the response of the component (peak values; the permanent settlement for approaches), from the database of Chen et al. (2025), Earthquake Spectra 41(4), doi:10.1177/87552930251343634, published on DesignSafe as PRJ-5910 (doi:10.17603/ds2-c73m-nj37, version 1, Open Data Commons Attribution License). The 25 models come from the 24 rows of EDP_Fragility Database.csv, which lists the median component capacities that the database associates with its Sa(1.0 s) curves; the Comments of the joint seal and Era 3 unseating models record where the published curves do not reflect them. Each model is a lognormal fragility function of that response, with the median capacity of the source and a dispersion of 0.35. Model IDs follow the pattern CRCB.<component>[.<qualifier>].<scope>.<source>. The qualifier appears only for Column models, where CD marks curvature ductility and DR drift ratio. The scope is a design era (E1 pre-1970, E2 1971–1990, E3 post-1991), SingleSpan for single-span bridges, MultiSpan for capacities that the database assigns to all six multi-span studies listed in Chen et al. (2025, Table 3), or an approach configuration (Step for a step offset; Slope10, Slope30, and Slope45 for a slope offset with a 10, 30, or 45 ft slab). The MultiSpan models do not cover the single-span bridge groups. The source token names the study the capacities come from: M17 for Mangalathu (2017), whose Table 6.13 holds the capacities that the database assigns to all six multi-span studies or to five of them; MCP18 for Mangalathu et al. (2018); MSJ17 for Mangalathu, Soleimani, and Jeon (2017); CPR22 for Cavalcante et al. (2022); and SXR22 for Shao et al. (2022). The demands are directional. They come from a structural analysis of the bridge, except the approach settlements, which come from a settlement analysis of the approach backfill. The EDP definitions follow Mangalathu (2017) Sec. 6.1, except for the column drift models, the two Cavalcante et al. (2022) models, and the approach models, whose Comments name the source of the definition. These models and the Sa(1.0 s)-based models of seismic/transportation_network/component/California RC Bridges 2025 and seismic/transportation_network/portfolio/California RC Bridges 2025 are alternative representations of the same damage; apply only one of them to a given bridge. The Comments of each model give the source of its capacities and every change to the published values: column drift converted from percent to ratio, and the one row that defines only the extensive and complete unseating states, represented here by two models whose slight and moderate states are set equal to extensive.

CRCB.AbAct.MultiSpan.M17.Description: Abutment fragility in terms of peak abutment active displacement for multi-span bridges of any era.
CRCB.AbAct.MultiSpan.M17.Comments:
DesignSafe PRJ-5910 v1, EDP_Fragility Database.csv, data row 10 (spreadsheet row 12), AbAct, EDP "Displacement (in.)"; source reference "All six listed in Table 3 of the paper".

The model gives the probability of reaching or exceeding each damage state as a lognormal function of the peak response of the component. The demand comes from a structural analysis of the bridge. The model uses the median capacity of the source and the dispersion of 0.35 that the database assigns to every EDP-based model. Each capacity applies to one unit of the component, and the demand is the response of that unit. The demand is directional (Demand-Directional 1), so it is supplied in the direction in which the EDP is defined, as a demand of type ABA at the location and direction of the component. These models and the Sa(1.0 s)-based models of seismic/transportation_network/component/California RC Bridges 2025 and seismic/transportation_network/portfolio/California RC Bridges 2025 are alternative representations of the same damage; apply only one of them to a given bridge. The EDP definition follows Mangalathu (2017) Sec. 6.1 and Table 6.1.

The capacities are those of Ramanathan (2012) Tables 5.14 and 5.17 as adopted by Mangalathu (2017) Table 6.13. The database assigns these capacities to all six multi-span studies listed in Chen et al. (2025, Table 3).

DS1.Description: Slight damage: aesthetic or minor functional damage to the abutment in the active direction, near first yield of the abutment piles; active abutment displacement exceeds a median capacity of 1.5 in.

DS2.Description: Moderate damage: major functional damage to the abutment in the active direction, near the ultimate deformation of the abutment piles; active abutment displacement exceeds a median capacity of 4 in.

CRCB.Approach.Slope10.SXR22.Description: Approach fragility in terms of permanent approach settlement for a 10 ft approach slab with a slope offset.
CRCB.Approach.Slope10.SXR22.Comments:
DesignSafe PRJ-5910 v1, EDP_Fragility Database.csv, data row 21 (spreadsheet row 23), Approach, EDP "Settlement (in.)"; source note "10 ft approach with slope offset"; source reference "Shao et al. (2022)".

The model gives the probability of reaching or exceeding each damage state as a lognormal function of the permanent settlement of the component. The demand comes from a settlement analysis of the approach backfill, as in Shao et al. (2022). The model uses the median capacity of the source and the dispersion of 0.35 that the database assigns to every EDP-based model. Each capacity applies to one unit of the component, and the demand is the response of that unit. The demand is directional (Demand-Directional 1), so it is supplied in the direction in which the EDP is defined, as a demand of type PAS at the location and direction of the component. These models and the Sa(1.0 s)-based models of seismic/transportation_network/component/California RC Bridges 2025 and seismic/transportation_network/portfolio/California RC Bridges 2025 are alternative representations of the same damage; apply only one of them to a given bridge. The EDP definition follows Shao et al. (2022).

The capacities are the Minor (LS2) and Moderate (LS3) settlement capacities of Shao et al. (2022, Table 2) for a 10 ft approach slab with a slope offset, converted from cm to inches. The study's Observable state, and its Major and Severe states where it defines them, are not included. In the study, the 10 ft approach slab represents early-designed bridges.

DS1.Description: Slight damage (the Minor state of Shao et al. 2022): rotation of the 10 ft approach slab from backfill settlement, with a slope change of about 1/80 to 1/40; approach settlement exceeds a median capacity of 2.1 in.

DS2.Description: Moderate damage (the Moderate state of Shao et al. 2022): rotation of the 10 ft approach slab from backfill settlement, with a slope change of about 1/40 to 1/20; approach settlement exceeds a median capacity of 4.2 in.

CRCB.Bearing.MultiSpan.M17.Description: Bearing fragility in terms of peak bearing deformation for multi-span bridges of any era.
CRCB.Bearing.MultiSpan.M17.Comments:
DesignSafe PRJ-5910 v1, EDP_Fragility Database.csv, data row 13 (spreadsheet row 15), Bearing, EDP "Displacement (in.)"; source reference "All six listed in Table 3 of the paper".

The model gives the probability of reaching or exceeding each damage state as a lognormal function of the peak response of the component. The demand comes from a structural analysis of the bridge. The model uses the median capacity of the source and the dispersion of 0.35 that the database assigns to every EDP-based model. Each capacity applies to one unit of the component, and the demand is the response of that unit. The demand is directional (Demand-Directional 1), so it is supplied in the direction in which the EDP is defined, as a demand of type BRD at the location and direction of the component. These models and the Sa(1.0 s)-based models of seismic/transportation_network/component/California RC Bridges 2025 and seismic/transportation_network/portfolio/California RC Bridges 2025 are alternative representations of the same damage; apply only one of them to a given bridge. The EDP definition follows Mangalathu (2017) Sec. 6.1 and Table 6.1.

The capacities are those of Ramanathan (2012) Tables 5.16 and 5.17 as adopted by Mangalathu (2017) Table 6.13. Mangalathu, Soleimani, and Jeon (2017, Table 4) give a moderate bearing capacity of 76 mm (3 in.) for the Era 1 bridges of that study, where this set has 4 in. The database assigns these capacities to all six multi-span studies listed in Chen et al. (2025, Table 3).

DS1.Description: Slight damage: aesthetic or minor functional damage to the elastomeric bearing pads; bearing deformation exceeds a median capacity of 1 in.

DS2.Description: Moderate damage: significant damage and tearing of the elastomeric bearing pads, which are replaced; bearing deformation exceeds a median capacity of 4 in.

CRCB.Column.CD.E1.M17.Description: Column fragility in terms of peak column curvature ductility for Era 1 (pre-1970) multi-span bridges.
CRCB.Column.CD.E1.M17.Comments:
DesignSafe PRJ-5910 v1, EDP_Fragility Database.csv, data row 0 (spreadsheet row 2), Column, EDP "Curvature ductility"; source note "For Era 1 bridges"; source reference "All six listed in Table 3 of the paper, except for Mangalathu et al. (2018)".

The model gives the probability of reaching or exceeding each damage state as a lognormal function of the peak response of the component. The demand comes from a structural analysis of the bridge. The model uses the median capacity of the source and the dispersion of 0.35 that the database assigns to every EDP-based model. Each capacity applies to one unit of the component, and the demand is the response of that unit. The demand is directional (Demand-Directional 1), so it is supplied in the direction in which the EDP is defined, as a demand of type CCD at the location and direction of the component. These models and the Sa(1.0 s)-based models of seismic/transportation_network/component/California RC Bridges 2025 and seismic/transportation_network/portfolio/California RC Bridges 2025 are alternative representations of the same damage; apply only one of them to a given bridge. The EDP definition follows Mangalathu (2017) Sec. 6.1 and Table 6.1.

The capacities are the Era 1 column curvature ductility capacities of Mangalathu (2017) Table 6.13, based on the review of column tests by design era in Sec. 6.1.2.1 and Table 6.11 of that thesis; Soleimani (2017) Table 7.5 gives the same values. The database assigns them to five of the six multi-span studies listed in Chen et al. (2025, Table 3), all but Mangalathu et al. (2018), whose curves use column drift. Soleimani, Mangalathu, and DesRoches (2017, p. 469) use column displacement ductility, not curvature ductility, as the column EDP; their curves in the database are system curves only.

DS1.Description: Slight damage: cracking of the column, repaired by sealing and painting; column curvature ductility exceeds a median capacity of 0.8 for Era 1 bridges.

DS2.Description: Moderate damage: minor spalling of the cover concrete, repaired by epoxy injection and minor concrete removal and patching; column curvature ductility exceeds a median capacity of 2 for Era 1 bridges.

DS3.Description: Extensive damage: exposed core and yielding of the transverse reinforcement; major repairs are needed, but the column keeps its function; column curvature ductility exceeds a median capacity of 5 for Era 1 bridges.

DS4.Description: Complete damage: longitudinal bar buckling, core crushing, or large drift; the column function is compromised and the column (or the bridge) is replaced; column curvature ductility exceeds a median capacity of 8 for Era 1 bridges.

CRCB.Unseating.SingleSpan.CPR22.Description: Span unseating fragility in terms of peak joint opening for single-span bridges of any era (groups E123-S1-C0-D and E123-S1-C0-S).
CRCB.Unseating.SingleSpan.CPR22.Comments:
DesignSafe PRJ-5910 v1, EDP_Fragility Database.csv, data row 6 (spreadsheet row 8), Unseating, EDP "Displacement (in.)"; source note "Bridge groups: E1-S2-C2P-S, E1-S3P-C2P-S, E123-S1-C0-D, E123-S1-C0-S"; source reference "Mangalathu, Soleimani, et al. (2017); Cavalcante et al. (2022)". The row lists four bridge groups and is represented here by two models with identical parameters: CRCB.Unseating.E1.MSJ17 for the two Era 1 groups (Mangalathu, Soleimani, and Jeon 2017) and CRCB.Unseating.SingleSpan.CPR22 for the two single-span groups (Cavalcante et al. 2022).

The model gives the probability of reaching or exceeding each damage state as a lognormal function of the peak response of the component. The demand comes from a structural analysis of the bridge. The model uses the median capacity of the source and the dispersion of 0.35 that the database assigns to every EDP-based model. Each capacity applies to one unit of the component, and the demand is the response of that unit. The demand is directional (Demand-Directional 1), so it is supplied in the direction in which the EDP is defined, as a demand of type JOP at the location and direction of the component. These models and the Sa(1.0 s)-based models of seismic/transportation_network/component/California RC Bridges 2025 and seismic/transportation_network/portfolio/California RC Bridges 2025 are alternative representations of the same damage; apply only one of them to a given bridge. The EDP definition follows Cavalcante et al. (2022).

The capacities are those of Cavalcante et al. (2022, Table 8), 152 and 229 mm (6 and 9 in.), for single-span bridges in northeastern Brazil, which Chen et al. (2025) use as a proxy for California single-span bridges.

The source defines unseating capacity for the extensive and complete states only. The slight and moderate medians are set equal to the extensive median; those two states cannot occur.

DS1.Description: Slight damage: not defined by the source; this state cannot occur (capacity set equal to extensive).

DS2.Description: Moderate damage: not defined by the source; this state cannot occur (capacity set equal to extensive).

DS3.Description: Extensive damage: seat displacement of more than about half the minimum seat width; joint opening exceeds a median capacity of 6 in. for single-span bridges.

DS4.Description: Complete damage: loss of seat support, with potential unseating of the span; joint opening exceeds a median capacity of 9 in. for single-span bridges.
